notes.title: Captain's Inn improvements, balance changes, expanded audio options and QoL!
notes.notes:
[h3][b]Ahoy me hearties! [/b][/h3]

Get ready to set sail once again – our second post-release update is live now!

Following on from the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2103470/view/4257672198526204531?l=english]roadmap [/url]which we shared earlier this month today’s update focuses on [b]improving the functionality of the captain’s inn[/b], [b]polishing the visuals of every captain’s portrait[/b], adding [b]more audio options[/b], and [b]addressing some of the balancing[/b], [b]QoL issues[/b] and bugs reported by the community.

[b]Captain’s Inn Improvements[/b]

This new update will give you much more flexibility when choosing which captain is worthy of joining your fleet. When visiting the captain’s inn, you will now be able to[b] re-roll the current offer of captains[/b], with a [b]2-minute cooldown[/b] between each selection. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/5d68021cb099e83596508fe109d6c98d48bb6fa1.gif[/img]

[b]New Captain’s Portraits[/b]

To more closely match the painted art style that is used elsewhere in the game, we have [b]reworked every captain’s portrait[/b]. Here’s a little sneak peek of the new painted versions that you can expect to see! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/b18eb5a622dd94d4b6184a2070e6433e17e38a40.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/bdee290bf128a9d7f69ed1b945989684c03e7459.png[/img]
[b]See the full list of patch notes below: [/b]

[b]New Features[/b]
[list]
[*] Captain re-rolling in the captain's inn with a 2-minute cooldown after each re-roll
[*] New captain’s portraits
[*] Volume sliders for shanties
[*] Volume sliders for battle music
[*] A warning message has been added to the input menu when attempting to reassign an input
[*] Borderless window lock options - can now move the cursor out of the window bounds to access other applications, such as Discord or Twitch
[/list]
[b]Bugs fixed[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with button prompts displaying incorrectly on the input menu (Russian)
[*] Fixed a text issue with the Free Trader reputation tooltip having the wrong values  for sinking trading company ships (German)
[*] Fixed an issue with the spawn location of the ships supposed to be attacking Hell's Gate Island
[*] Fixed an issue where players were unable to unlock new buildings
[*] Fixed an issue where worker needs were stuck at 99%
[*] Fixed an issue with the brass bar icon during trades
[/list]
[b]Balance changes[/b]
[list]
[*] Dried herbs production condition increased to 150% on Galley Island (Campaign)
[*] Dried herbs production condition increased to 150% on Arrecife Verde (Islas de Sangre free play map)
[*] Dried herbs production condition increased to 150% on Isla del Sable (Volcano Isles free play map)
[/list]
Stay tuned for more news regarding future updates – our next one is due to launch in early September and will introduce a new captain and fleet management UI which will allow for ship salvaging and more detailed captain management!   

Thank you all for your support and constructive feedback, we hope you’ll enjoy the new content and as always please do continue to post your comments in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2103470/discussions/0/4353373056334994167/]feedback thread[/url].

Fair winds and following seas,

Crazy Goat Games & PQube

notes.title: Update 9: Freeplay Mode
notes.notes:
[h2][b]Welcome back, pirates![/b][/h2]

After having focussed our attention on shipbuilding, fleet management, and diplomacy in our last few updates, we’re now going to dive into the different gameplay modes you’ll be able to experience at launch.

There are [b]two modes of play[/b] in Republic of Pirates –[b] campaign mode[/b] and [b]freeplay mode[/b], and today, we will teach you all about the differences between these modes, shine the spotlight on a couple of our freeplay maps and show you how progression works outside of campaign mode! 

[h3][b]New Horizons: Campaign and Freeplay Mode[/b][/h3]

Looking for a more [b]story-driven experience[/b]? Embark on an epic adventure in campaign mode and rebuild the once glorious Republic of Pirates. Your rag-tag crew of misfits will offer advice in the form of [b]tutorials[/b] which will aid you in progressing your story further. Follow the [b]main missions[/b] and [b]quest objectives[/b] to find out where your journey will lead you!

Begin your adventure on the [b]Forgotten Archipelago map[/b] and choose from three difficulties to customise your experience to your liking! 

Play in freeplay mode for a more [b]casual and open-ended experience[/b]. You will get the option to pick from[b] two additional maps[/b] with unique geography and layouts.
In freeplay mode, there are[b] no main missions to complete[/b], and gameplay will not be tutorialised. Instead, you will simply work to [b]grow your population[/b] and your republic while conquering the whole archipelago. 

How you play is ultimately up to you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/fe0424f5f4a576950b4fffb314c1c7047ba94d79.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]Freeplay Map Spotlight – Islas de Sangre[/b][/h3]

A balmy archipelago dominated by a central massive island covered in dense jungle. To the south-west lay five islands with a bloody history known as Las Cinco Hermanas, while to the east two trading lanes converge between a cluster of remote islets.

[b]Map Characteristics[/b]: An extra-large starting island with access to many rare resources. This island is situated further away from trade routes. All factions are active. 

[b]Starting Island Characteristics[/b]: A large island with two beaches

[b]Available Material Deposits[/b]: 
[list]
[*] Captain’s Inn Wreckage
[*] Zinc Deposit
[*] Salt Deposit
[*] Dried Herbs
[*] Crabs
[/list][b]Production Conditions:[/b]
[list]
[*] Fish -50%
[*] Hemp -50%
[*] Coal +50%
[*] Boars +50%
[*] Sugar +50%
[*] Aloe Vera +50%
[*] Boniatos -50%
[*] Tobacco +50%
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/7e80a168f05a349eb546910af5f2b20cf415a68e.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]Freeplay Map Spotlight - Volcano Isles[/b][/h3]

A rugged archipelago made up of volcanic islands and tropical atolls. Here the legacies of great pirate crews and nations intertwine to create a vivid tapestry of ambition and intrigue.

[b]Map Characteristics[/b]: A medium-sized starting island with access to some rare resources near a busy trade route. All major factions are active.

[b]Starting Island Characteristics[/b]: A medium-sized island with two beaches

[b]Available Material Deposits: [/b]
[list]
[*] Captain’s Inn Wreckage 
[*] Coal Deposit
[*] Salt Deposit
[/list][b]Production Conditions:[/b]
[list]
[*] Hemp +50%
[*] Fish +50%
[*] Boars +50% 
[*] Wood Logs +50%
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/4e1abca31f6779a782e1a6a37aff521c89a9b850.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]Freeplay Mode Map Difficulty[/b][/h3]

When playing on any of the freeplay maps, you will get to choose one of three difficulty modes. See below for the effects that are applied with each mode. 

[b]Easy[/b]
[list]
[*] Starting funds: 20.000 Doubloons
[*] Demolished buildings cost return: 100%
[*] Paused production building upkeep cost: 0% 
[*] Ship strength increased by: 50% 
[*] The number of available captains increased by: 3
[*] Random pirate attacks are less severe
[*] Increased income and decreased upkeep cost for selected buildings 
[*] Faction standing decreases at a reduced rate 
[*] Storage capacity increased by 15 
[/list]
[b]Medium [/b]
[list]
[*] Starting funds: 20.000 Doubloons
[*] Demolished building cost return: 100% 
[*] Paused production building upkeep cost: 0% 
[*] Ship strength increased by: 30% 
[*] The number of available captains increased by: 1
[/list]
[b]Hard[/b]
[list]
[*] Starting funds: 15.000 Doubloons
[*] Demolished building cost return: 80% 
[*] Paused production building upkeep cost: 20% 
[/list]
[h3][b]Cementing Your Legacy: Progression in Freeplay Mode[/b][/h3]

Despite giving you a pressure-free gaming experience, you’ll still have the opportunity to progress in freeplay mode. Contrary to the quest objectives you receive in campaign mode, your crew of misfits will no longer offer you main missions in freeplay mode. Instead, you’ll progress through the map by hitting [b]population milestones[/b]. Once you have reached a specific milestone, you will [b]unlock a new set of buildings[/b] which will ultimately allow you to develop your city further, and move onto the next population milestone and so on! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/4357a394cd37b3af4b6580ca5038eb8835e44ea7.gif[/img]

That’s all you need to know about freeplay mode for now. As usual, make sure to [b]wishlist Republic of Pirates[/b] and [b]follow us on social media [/b]to stay up to date on any news! 

Until next time!

notes.title: Update 8: Active Ship Skills
notes.notes:
[h2]Welcome back, everyone![/h2]

In our last few posts, we’ve given a detailed breakdown of how to manage your fleet, conquer the archipelago, and cultivate your relationships with other factions. 

Today, we’re excited to be revealing a [b]new combat mechanic [/b]in the form of [b]active ship skills[/b]. This recently implemented system will add an extra layer of strategy to naval battles and will make fleet building and composition even more impactful!

In[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2103470/view/6107508076986469993?l=english] update 4[/url] we looked at the role of the fleet, shipbuilding materials, ship classes, and customisation. 

To recap, you will [b]use your fleet to explore the archipelago[/b], and [b]attack merchants and rival pirate ships[/b]. In doing so, you will [b]receive valuable loot[/b] which will help you to [b]build more advanced ships [/b]and [b]conquer additional islands[/b]. By conquering more islands you’ll then gain access to rare resources and more land to expand your republic. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/92165710aa3a5c6b2720c29c9a1cf5ea986ecaf9.jpg[/img]
Remember that [b]every ship class has its own unique stat line[/b], but with the addition of the new active skills, you’ll need to be increasingly mindful of the importance of fleet composition and combat tactics when planning your next raid!

[h3][b]Man the Cannons: An Introduction to Active Skills [/b][/h3]

Depending on its class, each ship now has access to one of five active skills. These skills can be [b]triggered during combat [/b]by clicking on the ship and [b]selecting the active skill button[/b] in the ship unit UI. It's worth noting that if several ships have been group selected, you will also be able to see all their active skills at once and can easily choose the order in which they trigger, depending on your current needs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/7c88c709c966380cc62ff1cd55d05a7b2790d46e.jpg[/img]
[b]Active skills can be divided into three broad categories: [/b]

[list]
[*] [b]Offensive[/b]: Skills that directly attack and damage enemy units 
[*] [b]Disruptive[/b]: Skills that debuff enemy units in various ways
[*] [b]Support[/b]: Skills that buff allied ships 
[/list]
Once you have used an active skill, there will be a [b]short cooldown period[/b] before you will be able to use it again.[b] Cooldown times vary depending on the skill and the ship’s class[/b], so make sure to plan your attacks carefully. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/a5c73d2b4c898ba6f3c03f25c435f73e87c7a3fa.png[/img]

[i]See below for a full breakdown of the five skills.[/i]

[h3][b]Scattershot [/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Skill description[/b]: Fires a scattershot in a cone. It will hit all ships within the cone which can be rotated 360 degrees around the centre of the ship. The scattershot deals light damage. 
[*] [b]Skill type[/b]: Offensive 
[*] [b]Buildable ship class with skill[/b]: Cog, Brigantine 
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/300beadb00bd683c55cd9b124f602ab4afbb5359.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Smoke Bomb [/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Skill description[/b]: Fires a smoke bomb to a target location within range. This will create a small area of effect upon landing causing all enemy attacks from affected ships to miss for a short period. 
[*] [b]Skill type[/b]: Disruptive
[*] [b]Buildable ship class with skill[/b]: Ketch, Galleon
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/a5f685d89c6ad82f41100b21658b91b1f5df5c96.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Adjusted Sails [/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Skill description[/b]: Gives all nearby ships a temporary boost to their speed stat allowing them to traverse the map faster or escape from a difficult battle.
[*] [b]Skill type[/b]: Support
[*] [b]Buildable ship classes with skill[/b]: Frigate 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/b0856e164f2b8b0bd17535792a534477358c0bd6.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Shred Sails [/b][/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Skill description[/b]: Attack an enemy ship within range and damage their sails to slow them down for a limited time.
[*] [b]Skill type[/b]: Disruptive 
[*] [b]Buildable ship classes with skill[/b]: Brig 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/e696a7628e3ed156c38060815a9c55dc9a8e6a46.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Salvo[/b][/h3] 

[list]
[*] [b]Skill description[/b]: Unleashes a devastating attack on an individual enemy unit within range. Your unit will attack several times, inflicting massive damage on your enemy in a short period of time. 
[*] [b]Skill type[/b]: Offensive
[*] [b]Buildable ship classes with skill[/b]: Barque, Man-of-War 
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/fe657ebdfa9a4b4c2b3c76369305e3cab7e84052.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Steam demo announcement![/b][/h3]

On top of this new feature we’re really excited to announce that we will be launching our [b]Steam demo[/b] to tie in with [b]Steam Next Fest in June 2024[/b]! The exact live date for the demo is still TBC but until then, don’t forget to [b]wishlist the game [/b]and [b]follow us on our social media channels[/b] to stay up to date on any news! 

Until next time!

notes.title: Update 7: Managing Diplomacy
notes.notes:
[h2]Welcome back, pirates![/h2]

After having seen how to conquer the archipelago by force [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2103470/view/4157455695155236781][b]in our last update[/b][/url], it’s now time to learn about the consequences of your actions and reputation by doing a deep dive into diplomacy.

[b]PLEASE NOTE:[/b] While we are still working on the game, some of the terms, names, and quantities outlined below may be subject to change!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/a1bfd8506506ebf357e0b933963c8dbe0b1e6159.jpg[/img]

Expanding across the archipelago and conquering islands are crucial steps towards rebuilding the Republic of Pirates. At the beginning of your campaign, the majority of the map will be shrouded in a fog of war which will gradually lift the further you progress and acquire more territory. As you reveal new parts of the map, you will start to encounter and interact with more factions. 

So who are these mysterious forces?

[h3][b]Flying the Flag: An Introduction to Factions [/b][/h3]

There are[b] seven major factions[/b] in Republic of Pirates with three different standings; pirate clans, private traders, and national superpowers: 

[b]Pirate Clans[/b]
[list]
[*] Raiders of the Caribbean
[*] Los Guerreros 
[*] Gallows Men[/list][b]Private Traders[/b][list]
[*] Free Traders[/list][b]National Superpowers[/b][list]
[*] British West India Company 
[*] French Company of the Americas 
[*] Royal Barcelona Trading Company
[/list] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/56ea813e84129d308c1ca5454b19ed7f8da9a39c.png[/img]

[h3][b]Promises Made and Broken: An Overview of Diplomacy[/b][/h3]

Managing your relationships with each of the factions will be crucial to succeeding in your objectives and you can do this through the diplomacy menu. Click the [b]diplomacy icon on the left side of your screen[/b] to open the menu. Here you’ll get an overview of all the factions, your current standings with each of them, and the variety of diplomatic options available.

Faction standings are determined by a[b] relationship score that ranges between 0-100[/b]. These individual faction scores and associated standings will have various effects, such as how the faction reacts to your ships as well as their willingness to communicate and aid you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/df5a1c4dd598f948af344c769e77d42acf8d79b9.jpg[/img]
The effects linked to your current standing can be found below the faction relations bar. Hover over the question mark to learn how you can positively or negatively influence your relationship score.

A score between [b]0-20 equates to a bad standing[/b], leading to effects such as saboteurs infiltrating your settlements, superpowers raiding your islands, and faction aligned ships attacking your fleet on sight. 

A score between [b]20-80 means that a faction remains neutral[/b]. Depending on the type of faction, they may still make demands, allow for meetings to take place, and will likely appear far less hostile. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/3507009c02ada1379722288f7e10538971119365.gif[/img]

A score between [b]80-100 will grant you the positive effects of a good standing[/b]. This will open up a greater range of diplomatic options, and some factions may even lend their support to help defend your shores.

You will be able to [b]influence your standing through specific interactions[/b] with the factions. For example, destroying a faction’s ship or conquering one of their islands will negatively impact your standing, while attacking mutual rivals, accepting trade offers, fulfilling faction requests, and bribing a faction’s envoy count as positive actions. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/6074fa2aa4081c5ac1961b7fb7fdc8a36786f417.jpg[/img]
However, should you fail to fulfil or ignore a request your score will always be impacted negatively, so be prepared!

[h3][b]The Fine Art of Negotiation: Diplomatic Options[/b][/h3]

You will discover a variety of options to choose from in the diplomacy menu depending on the specific faction and your current standing with them. 

[b]Trade offers[/b]: Allow you to buy goods for a set amount of gold.

[b]Superpower requests[/b]: Used to boost reputation. The faction demands that you complete a mission within a limited time. Requests can be related to delivering goods or destroying enemy ships.

[b]Bribe envoy[/b]: The easiest way to boost reputation with a faction, and involves giving large quantities of money in exchange for goodwill. 

[b]Request aid[/b]: A special action for superpowers with positive relations whereby you can request allied ships to come help them defend your shores against another superpower's raid! 

[h3][b]Den of Thieves: An Overview of Pirate Clans[/b][/h3]

You are not the only pirate prowling the archipelago. The pirate clans of the Raiders of the Caribbean, Los Guerreros, and the Gallows Men, are the first obstacles that will likely block your progress as you seek to bring more territory under your control. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/41b1ef37f2fc2e40aaf807a59e9ec003a03e1ab1.jpg[/img]
Much like you, they have taken over islands which means you’ll need to [b]defeat their garrisons and fleets to continue your expansion efforts[/b]. They pose a [b]moderate threat [/b]throughout the game and can each be wiped out entirely with enough military pressure. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/0015682fe68cb9249c726939473aaf6efc506f1c.gif[/img]

While you can build up your relationship over time, you will likely have to deal with the negative effects of your conflict of interest. 

[b]Negative standing effects[/b]: Regular raids on your islands and attacking your ships on sight. 

[b]Neutral standing effects[/b]: Troublemakers and saboteurs present in your cities.

[b]Positive standing effects[/b]: Side quests offered.

[h3][b]Valuable Cargo: An Overview of Private Traders[/b][/h3]

In stark contrast to the aggressive pirate clans, you will frequently encounter the ships of the Free Traders. Unlike the pirate clans, they [b]own no islands and cannot be wiped out[/b]. Instead, they’ll peacefully sail through the archipelago along defined trading lanes, presenting valuable targets to opportunistic captains. In contrast to the other factions, the Free Traders will often prove to be more [b]utilitarian in function[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/434b28f99bb4427fbff533fd7e5476bde669a2de.jpg[/img]
[b]Negative standing effects[/b]: Less frequent ships along the trading lanes, and when they do appear, they will be accompanied by hostile escorts. Troublemakers and saboteurs present in your cities.

[b]Neutral standing effects[/b]: Trade offers will become available to further enhance your standing.

[b]Positive standing effects[/b]: Side quests offered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/f0e0028cbdd65294a809be5e53e9ca3dac7f287e.gif[/img]

[h3][b]For King and Country: An Overview of National Superpowers [/b][/h3]

Finally, the true powers in the Caribbean, three national superpowers: The British West India Company, the French Company of the Americas, and the Royal Barcelona Trading Company. 

These factions are incredibly powerful and can pose a [b]major threat[/b] to you and your Republic of Pirates.[b] Avoid attacking them at all costs[/b] and plan your actions carefully if you must take over one of their islands. Even once all of their islands are conquered, superpowers [b]cannot be eliminated[/b] from the game.

[b]Negative standing effects[/b]: Ships will attack your fleet on site, and in rare instances the superpower will launch a full blown raid, sowing a huge amount of destruction across one of your islands!  

[b]Neutral standing effects[/b]: Superpower requests will become available, but troublemakers and saboteurs will be present in your cities.

[b]Positive standing effects[/b]: Trade offers available, and request allied ships to defend your island when another superpower launches a raid. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/41b1708c3364beaa7518cab62fa5783614faf327.gif[/img]  

Your ability to navigate the complex web of diplomatic relationships will ultimately prove to be key to success, be conscious of your decisions as no action will go unnoticed in the archipelago! 

For now, that's all you need to know about diplomacy options in Republic of Pirates. As usual, make sure to[b] wishlist and follow[/b] us to stay up to date with news ahead of launch.

Until next time!

Crazy Goat Games & PQube

[h2]Welcome back, pirates![/h2]

To celebrate our inclusion in the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/balticshowcase][b]Baltic Showcase powered by DevGAMM and Digital Vikings[/b][/url], we’re back with another update post where we deep dive into one of the main mechanics of the game: conquest. 

In our last two posts we showed you how to build your fleet and recruit the very best captains to your cause, so now, it is finally time to set sail and conquer the archipelago! Let’s recap on [b]the importance of expansion[/b], learn how to [b]issue commands in and outside of the tactical map[/b], how [b]naval combat [/b]works, and how to [b]capture and defend islands[/b].

[b]PLEASE NOTE[/b]: While we are still working on the game, some of the terms, names, and quantities outlined below may be subject to change!

[h3][b]As Far as the Eye Can See: Expanding your Republic of Pirates[/b][/h3]

To rebuild the legendary Republic of Pirates, you will need to [b]focus on expanding your territory[/b]. Every conquerable island you discover possesses [b]several rare resources[/b] necessary to support the development of your pirate empire. By conquering more islands, you’ll subsequently gain access to those resources in addition to[b] acquiring more land[/b] to build on. [b]New Captain’s Inn spots[/b] will also become available once you have claimed certain key islands, allowing more captains to join your fleet. 

As you expand, you’ll swiftly[b] gain advantage over your rival factions[/b] by reducing their presence on the map. Create shipyards and docks on all available islands to strategically develop your fleet, protect your newly conquered land and launch additional raids. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/3fe9da048713d635a52ae9bfe355c1be01283650.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Setting Sail: Issuing Commands[/b][/h3]

Once you have built up your fleet, it's time to get those ships moving! Command your naval units to explore and conquer the archipelago through a [b]traditional move-and-fight system[/b]. Left-click on a ship to select it and right-click on a target (e.g. a waypoint, an enemy ship, an enemy building/defence tower, or flotsam) to issue the command. 

Want to issue the same order to more than one ship? No problem! [b]Drag-select a group of ships[/b] and right click on their intended target.

If you want to collect ship debris as efficiently as possible, [b]left-click on the collectable[/b] and the closest ship will move in to retrieve it. Using this method, you can also [b]select multiple waypoints[/b]!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/abafd0402ab9f44b9fbeb8cc17e6e9cbd0694ca1.gif[/img]

[h3][b]A Tactician’s Best Friend: Using the Tactical Map[/b][/h3]

The tactical map can be accessed anytime to get a [b]bird's eye view of the archipelago[/b]. From ship locations and patrol routes, to island overviews and side quests, you can gain a myriad of information from a quick look at the map. Inspect a location or unit by mousing over it to learn everything you need to know before planning your next move. 

Additionally, [b]units move in real-time[/b] when the tactical view is open so you can[b] issue commands on a macro level[/b] for a greater level of control. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/0c03ed175641fa8db2d14f94d569d99f1c77d60f.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]Battle Ready: An Overview of Naval Units [/b][/h3]

To succeed in conquering the archipelago you’ll first need to be familiar with the parameters that influence how your units perform in combat. Below you can find a breakdown of these key parameters: 

[b]Durability[/b]: These are the hit points of a unit. Once health has been depleted, the unit is destroyed!  

[b]Attack Range[/b]: This is how far the unit can fire its cannons. Higher tier ships typically have greater range than their lower tier counterparts.

[b]Speed[/b]: This is how fast the unit moves. Always consider the speed of your target as you may be able to utilise this to your advantage.

[b]Firepower[/b]: This is the damage inflicted with each shot. Higher tier ships possess the greatest firepower!

[b]Reload Time[/b]: This is the fire rate for a unit's cannons. Faster reload speeds mean higher damage per second.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/06c012b7450f3fc81c27be2e9d9a38024f5622c4.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]Smoke on the Water: An Overview of Naval Combat[/b][/h3]

Naval combat unfolds in real-time with combatants trading attacks until one is either destroyed or backs down. The aforementioned unit parameters – durability, attack range, speed, firepower, and reload time – along with the fleets involved, all influence how a battle unfolds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/43b2419522b27020d66259e953d4cdbb401211c9.gif[/img]

Should any of your ships get damaged in a fight, move them to a nearby docks building to [b]repair them using accumulated resources and gold[/b].

Any ships that you destroy will leave behind [b]valuable loot and rare materials[/b] which can in turn be used to build specific ship classes at your shipyard. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/3349c67b5f3a4dcefa6ec4b56369dec660490e15.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Friend or Foe: NPC Ship Behaviours[/b][/h3]

There are several types of NPC behaviour in Republic of Pirates. [b]Passive units[/b] will be portrayed in orange and will generally [b]allow your fleet to sail the archipelago freely[/b] unless attacked. Red and [b]aggressive NPC ships[/b], on the other hand, will [b]attack the player on sight[/b] without being provoked, so make sure to keep a distance unless you’ve come prepared for a fight! Lastly,[b] green ships[/b] are [b]allied and will fight against enemy targets[/b].

Check the [b]diplomacy screen[/b] to confirm your standing with the other major factions. Depending on your actions, you will either have achieved [b]hostile[/b], [b]neutral[/b], or [b]friendly[/b] standing all of which influence a faction’s behaviour towards you. Hostile factions, for example, will attack your ships on sight. Offer trade deals or fulfil missions in their name to rectify this. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/5e06565ccd3320610ffa8ed54702b52cdc0ace31.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Eyes on the Prize: Capturing Islands[/b][/h3]

Got your eyes on a specific island? Before you capture it, you must first destroy all rival vessels protecting its shores as well as any pre-existing infrastructure. Once cleared, you will be able to interact with your newly claimed island to gain an overview of its resources.

Place a docks building on the designated spot and begin your expansion!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/e5ffc1ec739dede7d3351622f2603ebd6caa4bd1.gif[/img]

[h3][b]A Double Edged Sword: Defending your Islands[/b][/h3]

The rival factions in Republic of Pirates are notorious for holding a grudge. Be wary of your enemies attacking your conquered islands as depending on your standing, they’ll likely launch,[b] frequent, small raids[/b]. Ensure that you manage your diplomatic relationships diligently or you might end up incurring the wrath of a superpower, who will launch a [b]devastating full-scale attack![/b] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/67c1b000d4973e3ad4ea5635b0d46a890d83c563.gif[/img]

If in doubt, check the diplomacy menu to learn more about your current relationships with the other factions. You’ll need to carefully[b] navigate a tense diplomatic environment[/b] in order to protect your hard won islands and fleet. 

Ultimately, you should always be prepared for an incoming attack, and in the absence of a fleet garrison, you can [b]build defence towers along each island’s shoreline[/b]. These towers can be upgraded across four tiers, increasing their durability and firepower with each subsequent tier. 

Should your defences fail, and a docks building be destroyed in an attack, you will lose a significant chunk of your gold reserves, and if you ever [b]reach -5000 gold, so ends your campaign[/b]! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/29c13d1b12854e90098abcfccb5dcc593ed40c17.jpg[/img]
That’s it for today, pirates! As always, make sure to [b]wishlist and follow Republic of Pirates[/b] to stay up to date on all news ahead of [b]launch this year[/b]. 

Until next time!

Crazy Goat Games & PQube

notes.title: Update 5: The Captain's Inn
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello there fellow pirates, it’s time for another update! [/h2]

In our last post, we delved into the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2103470/view/6107508076986469993][b]fleet building mechanics of Republic of Pirates[/b][/url], a crucial aspect of which being the recruitment and management of captains. Well, today we’ll be elaborating on these systems further! Discover [b]why captains are so important[/b], learn more about the [b]Captain’s Inn building[/b], [b]how to choose and assign your captains[/b], and more.

[b]PLEASE NOTE[/b]: While we are still working on the game, some of the terms, names, and quantities 
outlined below may be subject to change!

[h3][b]Chain of Command: The Importance of Captains[/b][/h3]

Your ships can’t navigate the archipelago without a trustworthy captain at the helm, and your fleet won’t grow unless you have enough captains waiting in the wings to lead a new crew. In gameplay terms, this means that [b]the total number of captains you can recruit at any one time will determine the number of ships[/b] you can field in your fleet. Captains can also learn [b]unique passive abilities [/b]that will allow them to develop interesting combat strategies and fleet compositions. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/752c923b984744fe7fc60d30ca89a074efda1254.png[/img]
To maximise the effectiveness of your fleet and successfully expand your pirate utopia, you’ll therefore need to[b] recruit a wide variety of captains[/b], pair them up with their ideal ship classes, and deploy them in the most advantageous conditions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/6f587b2007ec0469ff6a0ab9a6779328bffaa514.gif[/img]

[h3][b]A Hive of Scum and Villainy: The Captain’s Inn[/b][/h3]

Unlock the Shipbuilding category in the construction toolbar and look out for [b]Captain’s meeting places [/b]scattered across your conquered islands. These ruins hark back to the glory days of the former Republic of Pirates, and are [b]the only places where you can build a new Captain’s Inn[/b]. It's always worth scouting ahead to see which islands look interesting when planning your expansion, make sure to pay attention to rare resources and sites such as these! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/4a9c0fe68e243e42381dd3ecd80381ca3cc39a41.png[/img]
Once constructed, interact with the Captain’s Inn to find [b]a selection of four random captains to recruit[/b].

[h3][b]Under a Black Flag: Recruiting Captains[/b][/h3]

With four captains staying at the inn at a time you’ll need to decide which is the most suitable for your needs and budget. Each captain will have a [b]hiring fee[/b] which will differ based on their starting level as well as [b]three level milestones and associated skills[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/4501371a3e85c90a5c74fc887e30018c082578d0.jpg[/img]
Captains will hit their[b] milestones at levels 20, 30, and 40[/b] with each milestone unlocking a [b]permanent skill or passive buff[/b]. These skills can include a random chance to fire twice or increased performance when leading or attacking certain ship classes. 

[h3][b]Battle Ready: Assigning Captains[/b][/h3]

Ready to set sail? After you have hired your pirate captain, head to the shipyard and start building a new vessel. As the final step of shipbuilding, you’ll be prompted to assign an available captain to command your newly constructed ship, simple as! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/c4810af35bdfc3b29f7a3b345fd4a99fbd5d8956.png[/img]
[h3][b]Legends in the Making: Levelling Captains[/b][/h3]

Your captains will gain experience and expertise at sea and [b]level up automatically in naval combat[/b]. This means that the higher their initial level, the faster they will reach their skill milestones at levels 20, 30, and 40.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/dfd9f1fd7f9fdd839c747ab023da0cbee410e728.gif[/img]

Captain Sophia Delgado, for example, upon reaching level 20, will be rewarded with increased performance when leading a cog, ketch, or barque. At level 30, she’ll get a bonus for attacking rival ships of the same classes while her final skill will increase her performance when attacking any ship class. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/6a7a394592cd881e9ba0cad5824c8c5355005bc0.png[/img]

Ultimately you’ll need to think ahead as to how you want to build out your fleet and what you’ll be using it for! Is there a particular target you have in mind, or do you need a reliable local force to defend your shores?

That's all for now but please stay tuned for more community posts, and be sure to [b]wishlist Republic of Pirates[/b] before the game launches later this year! 

Until next time.

Crazy Goat Games & PQube

notes.title: Update 4: Building a Fleet
notes.notes:
[h2]Welcome back, pirates![/h2]

Today, we’re back with another update, just in time for [b]Pirates vs Ninjas Fest[/b]! 

In this post we’ll be looking at how to build a fleet in [i]Republic of Pirates[/i], providing [b]an overview of the shipyard, shipbuilding materials, ship classes and customisation. [/b]

[b]PLEASE NOTE[/b]: While we are still working on the game, some of the terms, names, and quantities outlined below may be subject to change!

[h3][b]The Open Seas: Why Your Fleet Matters[/b][/h3]

A pirate is nothing without their vessel, and in both campaign and freeplay mode, a strong fleet will be essential for expanding your influence across the archipelago and completing important quest objectives. Once you have a few ships under your command, you can strike out in search of loot and flotsam, engage in real-time naval combat with your rivals, conquer neighbouring islands, and defend your shores against enemy raids. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/e731ac7fac4da1e144ef8acf7131879d85567ec8.gif[/img]

[h3][b]The Shipyard: It All Starts Here[/b][/h3]

The shipyard building is the epicentre of fleet construction. Place it on any available shoreline belonging to your island(s) to get started. Within the shipyard building UI, you’ll be able to select the ship class of your choice, assign it a captain you have recruited, customise its cosmetics through unlocked sail and hull patterns, and begin construction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/3e9cb1c5260162655e9d11c61ee78a54cc771027.png[/img]
[h3][b]A Fleet in the Making: Shipbuilding Materials [/b][/h3]

As you progress through [i]Republic of Pirates[/i], you’ll unlock eight different ship classes which, due to their varying size and power, will require different materials in order to be constructed. Four out of the eight hull classes make use of resources that you can supply using the production buildings within your own settlements, while the others require materials that are looted from destroyed enemy vessels.  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/e3a9f0d158a778333320e3610c4adf79f75f6624.gif[/img]

We have created an overview to give you an idea of the variety of materials you’ll need to start building below:  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/44e81eda9056114ad8b7f59830e0233a22e1d418.png[/img]

[h3][b]Shipshape and Bristol Fashion: An Overview of Ship Classes[/b][/h3]

As mentioned, you’ll have a total of eight ship classes which you will be able to build once you have gathered the necessary materials. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/e844d33d952064b0306a66c5f5920fd5e65ec395.png[/img]
If you’re looking to build the top tier Galleon and Man-Of-war you’ll also need an additional building in the form of the advanced shipyard, so make sure you plan ahead! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/f71c2fef50630169ae8fda074f23ef154eeda94a.png[/img]
All ships vary in appearance and stats so you can experiment with different combinations and develop new compositions to suit your strategy.

We’ll give you a brief overview of six of the eight ship classes while the remaining two tiers, are still being implemented. 

[b]Cog[/b]: The cog is the first ship you’ll build as you begin your pirate adventure. Although the cog represents the lowest ship tier, compared to the other ships in the shipyard, its maintenance cost and construction time are significantly lower. 
[list]
[*] Firepower: 65, Speed: 6, Reload time: 2, Health: 780, Range: 34 (Maintenance cost: 10 Gold)[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/278421604b15a94bb75360594d51b4eba8fb510f.png[/img]
[b]Ketch[/b]: The ketch is the first ship you will need to outsource materials for but with its upgraded speed, firepower, and health the additional effort will be worth it.

[list][*] Firepower: 78, Speed: 7, Reload time: 2, Health: 1040, Range: 34 (Maintenance cost: 15 Gold)[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/8d318c642acb1821e31ed7a6cb2e06f7111a4398.png[/img]
[b]Barque[/b]: As a big step up from the first two tiers, the barque comes with more than double the health and almost twice the firepower of the ketch. This class can now lead your fleet and is perfect for targeting larger enemy ships.

[list][*] Firepower: 169, Speed: 8, Reload time: 2, Health: 2600, Range: 34 (Maintenance cost: 50 Gold) 
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/bf7edca82069733e78418ad99c2c1c9ba5221606.png[/img]
[b]Brig[/b]: Add a brig to your fleet for just a few extra coins and up your firepower and health.

[list][*] Firepower: 203, Speed: 9, Reload time: 2, Health: 3380, Range: 34 (Maintenance cost: 60)[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/45deda19ec5a6b911d399990970fda9575f47aea.png[/img]
[b]Brigantine[/b]: Upgrade your fleet by building a brigantine. With increased firepower, speed, and range, this ship class is perfect for laying siege to rival islands. 

[list][*] Firepower: 325, Speed: 11, Reload time: 2, Health: 4550, Range: 36 (Maintenance cost: 150)[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/204f8fa73624af0f7ad7f1445895d22dd4da3aa9.png[/img]
[b]Frigate[/b]: The bigger the better! With the highest firepower and health, very few will dare and stand in the way of a fleet led by your frigate. 

[list][*] Firepower: 390, Speed: 11, Reload time: 2, Health: 5005, Range: 36 (Maintenance cost: 170)[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/f00b18d4ba98006d30e9b31bc4da968f7bcb81a8.png[/img]
[h3][b]Flying Your Flag: Customisation Options [/b][/h3]

Customise your fleet to your heart’s desire! Unlock over 30 hull colours, sail patterns and insignia by completing missions and subjugating your rivals.

Do you prefer a uniform fleet or a mix-and-match of patterns and colours? Choose your favourite ship designs in the shipyard! It's worth noting that all customisation options in the shipyard are entirely unique and cannot be found on any other ships but yours!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/9489caa169a787ab8d1520285f3cb490f291092a.png[/img]
[h3][b]Command Your Crew: Assigning a Captain [/b][/h3]

Scour your islands for a captain’s meeting spot and construct a captain’s inn to begin attracting and recruiting veteran sailors to your cause. Remember, every ship must have its own captain so pay attention to their starting level, skills, and recruitment costs before you assign them. Depending on the difficulty setting, the number of recruitable captains will vary, and you can check the maximum available capacity at the captain’s inn. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/d4b60ff97de7cc61c9c222fa4f1be66a40d041d8.png[/img]
[h3][b]A Fresh Coat of Paint: Ship Repainter Building [/b][/h3]

Changed your mind about a ship’s design? Once unlocked, head over to the ship repainter building to change cosmetic options for ships that have already been built! 

Simply place the ship repainter on a shoreline and move your ship within range to change its hull colour, sail patterns and insignia in exchange for a few gold coins. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/56f18791548d285201c7c8795d0e9f2ab29a21b1.png[/img]
For now, that's all you need to know about building and expanding your fleet in [i]Republic of Pirates[/i]. We hope you have enjoyed today’s post and we’ll be back in a few weeks time with another update. 

Until next time!

Crazy Goat Games & PQube

notes.title: Update 3: Expanding the Workforce
notes.notes:
[h3]Welcome back, everyone![/h3]

[b]Steam’s Capitalism and Economy Fest[/b] starts today and to celebrate our participation we’re back with another update! In our last few posts we discussed the fundamentals of establishing a pirate utopia and the city building mechanics linked to creating a resource-based economy. Today we’ll be taking a closer look at your pirate citizens and expanding your workforce. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/c5d441f57040897b4979aa7d224e2ae96ce2de14.jpg[/img]
We’ll highlight the value of citizens to your growing economy, provide an overview of housing and citizen tiers, break down the requirements needed to upgrade each tier and provide examples of buildings that each require different types of workers. 

[b]PLEASE NOTE[/b]: While we are still working on the game, some of the terms, names, and quantities outlined below may be subject to change!

[h3][b]Labour and gold: The Importance of Citizens [/b][/h3]

Your Republic of Pirates won’t function without its citizens and growing the population of every one of your islands will come with important advantages:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/f1891f1d432efb0bf97b03670a762ffd478c1b55.png[/img]

[b]Providing a local workforce[/b]: Every island you conquer will have its own local workforce that will be employed in buildings located on that island. The bigger the workforce employed in each building, the more efficiently it will operate.  
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/516435502b6782a83bd3bd3a6503c59b79ded55b.jpg[/img]
[b]Generating income[/b]: Each citizen tier will provide a base level of global gold income that can be boosted by supplying requested resources, luxuries, and access to services.   

To keep your economy afloat, you’ll therefore need to balance your global population and supply chain with local availability of higher tier and more specialised workforces. Remember every production and service building in your republic will have a maintenance cost so keep an eye on your incomes and outgoings to ensure steady growth.

[h3][b]Living in luxury: Housing and Citizen Tiers[/b][/h3]

Big things often have small beginnings, so when initially building up your island you’ll begin by constructing low-tier houses for your pirate citizens before moving on to more luxurious dwellings. Each housing tier provides the following population and income range dependent on the resources and services that are provided:

[b]Tier 1 housing[/b]

Population range: 0-10 citizens 
Income range: 0-10 gold coins

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/8a4fe74428c1d70f672aad0117dc65d2cbcd3198.jpg[/img]

[b]Tier 2 housing[/b]

Population range:  0-20 citizens 
Income range: 8-43 gold coins

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/232e0cad381123a63af688a51ac8b3bca9132732.jpg[/img]

[b]Tier 3 housing[/b]

Population range:  0-30 citizens 
Income range: 44-141 gold coins

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/42a2c28c804ccdb79ea0f0cddd5ec709070b3c1b.jpg[/img]

[b]Tier 4 housing[/b]

Population range:  0-40 citizens 
Income range: 120-347 gold coins

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/43cb83e96525eb6e6d0d810a5c154e9496ab3df3.jpg[/img]

Naturally the citizen tier of a worker depends entirely on which one of the housing tiers they inhabit. In Republic of Pirates, different tiers of workers are required to operate specific buildings which in turn are necessary for sustaining and developing your economy. So a lumber mill and a candle maker, will require distinct groups of workers to operate! 

[h3][b]Levelling up: Housing Tier Requirements[/b][/h3]

Upgrading your housing is crucial for providing the necessary workers for different types of production buildings. Although the upgrade requirements for housing tiers differ depending on their current level, existing needs are cumulative. This means that if you want to keep upgrading you’ll need to sustain the availability of previously fulfilled basic needs as well as introducing new ones!  The main thing to remember is that in order to raise your housing tier, ALL basic needs must be met. Fulfilling luxury needs will simply provide income bonuses. 

Below we’ll provide a breakdown of the necessary basic needs which are required to upgrade between housing tiers as well as luxury needs to show how to best maximise your income per residence:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/e6328fcc61fcf57a9805c3a6aa13b697c32221b1.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/f3d8eb03769db6fb2c6615cea37669ef5cb5bbe4.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/1415666c1cb4a6f892dfa250e7850e90ac41fc3f.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/7b7c43b901acfd15898bbbb33d257f81d6eb6ef6.png[/img]

[h3][b]Diversified economy: Example workforces[/b][/h3]

Each production and service building in Republic of Pirates will require a specific number and tier of workers in order to function and accomplish peak performance. The quantity and quality of workers necessary will depend entirely on how advanced the building is! Some examples below:   

[b]Lumber mill[/b]: The lumber mill is a basic production building that refines wood harvested from lumberjacks into timber which is used in the construction of buildings and ships. At the height of production, it will employ 50 tier 1 workers. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/c88a1c078229fdecb3e552b3e62aedce4ff23301.jpg[/img]

[b]Candle Maker[/b]: As the last building in an intermediate production chain, this building supplies your settlement with candles, basic needs for tier 2 housing. The candle maker requires 50 tier 2 workers to operate at peak performance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/9b5e743e9f8766bf97522c31136ff5ad661ca79c.jpg[/img]

[b] Ironwood Carver[/b]: Sitting at the end of an advanced production chain, the ironwood carver supplies ironwood planks sourced from processed raw ironwood. To achieve this product, which is used for constructing  higher-level ships, the ironwood carver should ideally employ 75 tier 3 workers. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/24837e1905ed06e91fed1ee94ac33e8436667a62.jpg[/img]

[b]Astrolabe[/b]: Your highest tier workers will be employed to craft complex navigational devices like the astrolabe, a scientific instrument used to, among other things, observe heavenly bodies. As a basic need for tier 4 residences, this building requires 100 tier 4 workers to function efficiently.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/1d2dad7c884c76b1a35c8e545b904b490c0651e8.jpg[/img]

That’s just a taste of some of the buildings you’ll be deploying your workforce to, there will be 100+ buildings and décor items to construct and maintain in the final release!

We hope you’ve enjoyed today’s post, and we’ll be back in a few weeks with another update.
Until next time! 

Crazy Goat Games & PQube

notes.title: Update 2: Creating a Resource-Based Economy
notes.notes:
[h3]Welcome back, pirates![/h3]

In our last update we got to know the history of the Republic of Pirates, the main objectives you’ll be working towards in Campaign mode, an overview of the archipelago map, and even enjoyed a first look at freeplay mode. Today, we’ll be exploring the mechanics you’ll need to master in order to [b]build and maintain a successful resource-based economy[/b]. 

Specifically we’ll focus on the city-building aspect of Republic of Pirates and explain [b]why resources matter[/b], take a look at the[b] building categories [/b]at hand, demonstrate [b]how to set up production chains[/b] and show you [b]how to store and transport your resources[/b]. There’s lots to learn!

[b]It’s Time to Start (City) Building[/b]

Expanding your settlements across different islands is the key to building a successful pirate utopia. Not only will conquering islands provide strategic footholds across the archipelago but it will also provide land to radically grow your population and unique resources to feed into increasingly more complex production chains. This will increase the number of goods you’re able to supply, allowing you to [b]upgrade your pirate citizenry[/b], [b]construct more powerful ships[/b] for your fleet, and [b]heighten your chances of fulfilling trading missions[/b] with other factions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/4a7c249a928c2fdd2d245234c1823ca9dcf7d914.png[/img]
[b]Thoughtful city planning and building[/b] is therefore at the heart of developing your resource-based economy. Balance your income against maintenance costs, keep a close eye on the flow of goods between production buildings, and maintain a diverse workforce to keep your settlements ticking!

[b]Why Resources Matter[/b]

Resources are used in a wide variety of ways and are organised into a number of key categories: 
[list]
[*] [b]Needs[/b] resources (e.g. dried fish and rum) are used to fulfil the basic and luxury needs of your pirate citizens. Fulfilling basic needs will increase population and income per residence, while accommodating luxury needs will provide a significant income bonus. 
[*] [b]Production[/b] resources (e.g. hemp and cotton) are required to feed other production buildings to produce more advanced goods and luxuries.
[*] [b]Building[/b] materials (e.g. timber and bricks) are needed along with gold coins collected through taxation to construct new buildings.
[*] [b]Shipbuilding[/b] materials (e.g. sails and cannons) are used in combination with building materials to construct new ship units at the shipyard. 
[/list]
As previously mentioned, resources can be used to complete trade missions with rival powers. This will not only help you gain valuable resources for your own settlement but will improve your relationship with the respective faction. 

[b]Living off the Land: Types of Building Categories [/b]

Like resources, city building options are organised into key categories in the construction toolbar for ease of navigation. As you complete campaign and freeplay missions, new buildings will be added to each category, so check back regularly to see how your options are developing! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/2034d98fa21f7e8a162e483b1730a7f3bebb134e.png[/img]
[b]City[/b]: Your settlement won’t get very far without any citizens and an efficient courier system. This category forms the basis of your pirate utopia and includes housing, roads, storage, and logistics buildings.

Build and upgrade huts to house your citizens and[b] create a source of income through taxation[/b]. Storage buildings can be used to [b]stockpile materials and distribute goods to nearby buildings[/b], and are therefore crucial for setting up production chains. Lastly, no pirate settlement is complete without a dock which is used to claim a new island, share global resources between islands, and repair damaged ships. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/c7519e2d4751faccdcbae0d6d93bcf5920a1d6af.png[/img]
[b]Needs[/b]: Produce and refine resources to [b]fulfil your citizens’ basic needs[/b] with the help of the production buildings available in this category. Your pirate citizens will demand a variety of resources in order to improve their standing (and taxes!).

While fisheries produce dried fish ready for consumption, hemp plantations and rope makers will work in sequence to manufacture rope, indispensable for fleet building. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/d94931fae7fa094041300abc1163e0933798998a.png[/img]
[b]Luxuries[/b]: Your hardworking pirate citizens deserve to have a comfortable life. Build a sugar plantation and rum distillery to lift their spirits or repurpose the cotton used in sailsmaking at a hammock maker to add a sparkle of luxury to everyday life in your Republic. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/aa8a5274e0941ac87f68d77066917d3d23411fc5.png[/img]
[b]Services[/b]: Pirates are used to a hard life on the seas, so any additional landbound comfort you can provide is greatly appreciated! Provide [b]specialised service buildings that fulfil citizenry needs[/b] via an area of effect.

The black market is the heart of your settlement distributing goods to citizens living nearby, while taverns and brothels will support population growth and increase income by providing entertainment for your community. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/3d37023ab33b7902de00a9501f551bb94a5dbd10.png[/img]
[b]Materials[/b]: To sustain its economy, your Republic of Pirates needs to always be producing and refining construction materials. If not development will falter, your fleet will fail to expand, and trade deals cannot be struck, so make sure to keep on top of these production chains to [b]prevent an economic breakdown[/b]. 

With each island having its own [b]inherent resource advantages[/b], you’ll have to consider where best to place your lumbermills, brick kilns, and iron mines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/fcf8936f017908711727e663f13e5d59ceeccb63.png[/img]
[b]Seafaring[/b]: In order to take to the waves and conquer the archipelago, you’ll need to get acquainted with the seafaring category. 

[b]Produce a range of ships[/b] in the shipyard,[b] customise their classes and designs[/b] and let your fleet set sail! Place the captain’s inn on your island and [b]recruit heroic captains [/b]to lead your fleet. But where there is successful piracy, there will be rivalry. Protect your island from unwanted attention by [b]building upgradeable defence towers[/b] to automatically attack enemy ships venturing too close to your shores.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/51be14e9d9a53fc9fa755767478387823c506a3c.png[/img]
[b]Decor[/b]: Although they don’t provide any direct benefits to your settlements, decor items can be built to add character! From pirate monuments to figureheads and anchor statues, exhibit the fruits of your voyages and get creative with their placement to make each island unique!

[b]Production Chain Examples [/b]

Production chains are one of the main mechanics of Republic of Pirates, and while they are easy to set up, can become incredibly complex as you progress further into the game. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/c5dce566c55c6a1ffdfeb7704d2bee36c4422a65.png[/img]

At its core, [b]a production chain takes one or several ‘raw’ materials and turns them into a ‘refined’ resource[/b]. A basic example of this would be using the hemp grown in your hemp plantation to manufacture rope at the ropemaker. This works similarly for all major resources such as lumber, sails, rum, etc. which can only be produced if enough of their respective raw materials are available.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/c817049ccf2ab057c480754731ff6ef9a9fb75ae.png[/img]

Sometimes, if you’re looking to produce luxury goods or more intricate materials like metal, you will find that [b]production chains become much more complex.[/b] At this stage, they will involve [b]three or more buildings[/b] which all work in sequence to deliver the final product. In the case of steel beam production, the production chain will look like this: Coal produced in the charcoal kiln and iron produced in the iron mine can both be used for steel production in the furnace which consequently enables the steelwork to produce steel beams. 

[b]Storing and Distributing Resources[/b]

Once produced, you can rely on couriers to [b]transport your goods to storage buildings[/b]. Storage outposts can be placed strategically to[b] link production buildings, production chains, and black markets[/b] in range to create an efficient flow of goods. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/c32f138e73bf04c512b119b2abee1240fa646433.png[/img]
Docks link together conquered islands, allowing them to [b]share global resources [/b]with one another. Your Republic of Pirates will have an [b]initial global storage capacity per resource which can be increased by constructing storage sheds. 
[/b]
Similarly individual production buildings have their own individual storage caps that can be upgraded using gold and additional construction materials.

We hope you now have a better insight as to how you’ll set up your own resource-based economy when [b]Republic of Pirates launches in 2024[/b]! In our next post we’ll be taking a closer look at the workforce, citizen and housing tiers.

Until next time!

Crazy Goat Games and PQube

notes.title: Update 1: Establishing a Pirate Utopia
notes.notes:
[h3][b]Welcome to the Republic of Pirates![/b][/h3]

Today, as the first part of our regular community update series, we’ll be talking you through [b]how to create your very own pirate utopia [/b]in our upcoming pirate-themed city builder and real-time strategy game Republic of Pirates! So that you can hit the ground running and watch your settlements flourish when the game releases, we’ll be giving a summary of [b]the story so far[/b], your [b]main objectives in Campaign mode[/b], an overview of the [b]archipelago map,[/b] and a [b]first look at freeplay mode[/b]!   

[b]The Story So Far: What is the Republic of Pirates? [/b]

[b]At the heart of the Caribbean during the Golden Age of Piracy[/b] sat a powerful league of pirate clans, collectively known as the [b]Republic of Pirates[/b]. Bound together by a shared ideology and code of honour the early years of the confederacy were prosperous. However, greed and jealousy soon took hold amongst its more ‘ambitious’ members, leading to a vicious mutiny and[b] final bloody breakup[/b].  

In campaign mode, this is where your story begins as you set out to [b]reclaim your murdered father’s legacy by reforging a new republic[/b], subjugating your rivals, and bringing justice to the traitors who wronged you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/ad7e0a11207b3c2bec24bc140835570b0eb365c0.png[/img]
[b]Sand, blood, and gold: An Overview of Campaign Mode[/b]

[b]Campaign mode is your gateway into the world of Republic of Pirates[/b] and the very first place you should start, providing[b] helpful tutorials for all the major game mechanics[/b], while also setting you on a narrative-driven mission to [b]grow your humble settlement [/b]into a sprawling, archipelago-spanning utopia!
Your main objectives will be centred around [b]creating a self-sustaining economy[/b], [b]growing your population[/b], and [b]expanding your influence across a number of key islands[/b]:

[b]Creating a self-sustaining economy[/b]: By constructing production buildings and setting up production chains you’ll be able to [b]produce and refine resources[/b], which in turn can be distributed via couriers amongst your pirate citizenry through[b] a network of carefully planned storage warehouses, docks, and black markets.[/b] As your economy develops, you’ll discover increasingly more [b]advanced buildings with ever more complex chains[/b], so careful city planning will be key to ensuring that buildings receive adequate resource supplies.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/eef39ed09eb1642a08d445461b63e2df73e61ff0.png[/img]
[b]Growing your population[/b]: The citizens of your burgeoning republic will act as both your main source of income, and your workforce. Provide housing for your citizens and supply them with resources to [b]fulfil their basic and luxury needs[/b]. Accommodating basic needs will [b]increase population per residence [/b]and allow you to[b] upgrade your citizens[/b] to the next tier. If you’re also able to fulfil luxury needs you’ll [b]gain more income per citizen [/b]so try to make sure that you’re giving your pirates the very best quality of life! More advanced buildings will require increasingly skilled workers, be mindful of this when planning out your residential areas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/30e86256d5ed9977a107c840e7b4100cd4fd510d.png[/img]
[b]Expanding your influence[/b]: Each island in the archipelago will have [b]unique production conditions[/b] which give bonuses and penalties for the production of certain resources, while also [b]providing limited access to rare materials[/b]. This essentially means that to keep growing you’ll need to discover and bring new islands under your control. Construct vessels for your fledgling fleet at the Shipyard, and visit the Captain’s Meeting Spot to recruit heroic captains to crew your ships, before taking to the waves in the name of conquest! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/0c234114807047a99a28d4577b0598eac9d64446.png[/img]
[b]Trouble in paradise: Exploring the Archipelago[/b]

The main way that you will be exploring the archipelago in campaign mode will be through the [b]tactical map,[/b] a view that gives a[b] real-time snapshot of the major and minor islands[/b] that you have discovered, as well as the live positions of allied, neutral, and rival faction ships and bases. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/a350aec3ae0229b38a8aae01c05863a618fbd388.gif[/img]

From this view you can scout out islands by mousing over them to[b] reveal their production conditions, available rare resources, and the faction currently in control[/b].  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/e0f0c248db4fa2c493c56675c1b1c5edc5c3d072.png[/img]
Most importantly your fleet can be given commands in this view with [b]ship movement tracking in real-time[/b], enabling you to[b] plan your raids effectively[/b] and [b]pre-empt or respond to enemy attacks[/b]. 

While conquering minor islands will provide access to new resources and staging posts for launching the next phase of your expansion,[b] major islands will act as key milestones[/b] in your mission to reunite the archipelago under a single black flag.    

Be warned though as [b]no action will go unnoticed[/b], and your decisions will influence the attitudes of rival pirate clans and national superpower factions to your benefit and detriment. You’ll therefore need to navigate and actively[b] manage complex diplomatic relationships[/b] in order to keep expanding!

The fate of the Republic of Pirates is yours to shape!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44771533/1661b754653c1a54f995ed11383106b56aee1dbe.png[/img]
[b]Writing your own legend: Freeplay Mode[/b]

For those looking for a more relaxing experience, at launch, the strategy city builder will also feature a [b]freeplay mode with two additional maps[/b] to explore. Stay tuned for more updates on this new gameplay mode in later Steam posts!

That’s it for today, pirates. We hope that’s been helpful for giving you a good overview of how you will be establishing your pirate utopia. Over the coming months, we’ll be releasing a regular series of posts taking a closer look at specific mechanics and features!

Republic of Pirates is [b]coming to Steam in 2024[/b], so[b] wishlist and follow now [/b]and be the first in the know.

Until next time!

Crazy Goat Games & PQube
